page: Amazon Web Services r8i.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 4 vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

The underlying x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2109.87 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1890.0. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4363.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 4286.46. Single-threaded gzip compression is a notable strength, registering at 33.41 GB/sec.

Despite its memory-optimized classification and DDR5 memory generation, the instance exhibits weak memory bandwidth in large-block read and write tests, measuring 31.47 GB/sec and 17.95 GB/sec respectively. Passmark memory and database operations scores also fall into the lower tier. For workloads involving Redis, the instance achieves an average throughput of 7.49 million SET operations per second. Small-model LLM inference runs at average speeds, but text generation for 7B models drops to a poor 4.56 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8i.xlarge provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio on modern DDR5 hardware, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require high multi-core compute density. Appropriate workloads include single-threaded data processing, text processing, caching layers like Redis, and lightweight web serving.
